prerequisites: Complex numbers (real part, imaginary part, modulus and phase)
Fundamental principles of mechanics (energy conservation, fundamental principle of dynamics)

learning_outcomes.text: Become familiar with the basic concepts of electrokinetics: electric current and resistance, electromotive force, methods of analyzing electrical networks, electrical networks in transient regime, and in forced sinusoidal regime.
Identify a question within a disciplinary field (Propose analogies, make order-of-magnitude estimates and grasp their meaning, Manipulate the main mathematical tools useful in physics).
Analyze a question by mobilizing disciplinary concepts (Mobilize fundamental concepts to model, analyze and solve simple physics problems).
Qualitatively understand the functioning of an electrical installation.
Be able to calculate the different relevant electrical quantities in permanent and sinusoidal operating regimes.
Master the main characteristics of ideal dipoles (R, C, L, generators).
Build a simple electrical circuit and connect measurement instruments (oscilloscope, voltmeter).
Be able to understand the physical origin of electric charges and model them.
Be able to use the principle of charge conservation in simple examples.
Be able to understand the origin of the electrostatic field, analytically relate it to the concept of electric charge, and calculate the electrostatic field created by simple charge distributions.
Be able to implement Gauss's theorem in simple examples.
Be able to calculate the potential energy and the electrostatic potential.
Be able to understand the physical origin of electric current, current density, and model these two quantities.

syllabus_topics: Electric field created by fixed charges: the electrostatic field
Field created by a point charge
Field created by a continuous charge distribution
